Edition theme

Feel first

Tactile, intuitive, joyful – design pushing back on the screen

Three days, one mood: design reaching for what can be felt rather than scrolled. Mother Design began Purple Garden’s rebrand with a séance and charcoal drawings; Elmwood held a digitally rebuilt Dolmio puppet family to the standard of the handmade originals; odd works pitched Toyto’s wooden blocks against the blue light of screens; and at Nothing, former Loewe CMO Charlie Smith is doubling down on “joy and wonder”. Comebacks continue, now as a named pattern – Argos’s catalogue mascots, Aldi’s Kevin the Carrot and high-street brands courting luxury. Swiss Typefaces spent three years on a Swiss Post font designed to go unnoticed. On the business side, Canva has cut jobs as it navigates the shift to AI, Interbrand’s ranking has Hermès and Zara up and Nike down, and Saudi Arabia’s Ithra Design Week has been cancelled for 2026.

The lead · Rebrands & New Identity

How a séance shaped Purple Garden’s rebrand

Creative Bloq · 31 Oct · Mother Design for Purple Garden

Mother Design began rebranding Purple Garden, the online psychic services platform, with a séance, a chakra reading and an automatic drawing workshop. Working instinctively with paper and charcoal, the team tried to bypass conscious thought – and those forms became the basis of the identity.

Why it matters: a rebrand for a category built on intangibles, run on a process to match. Mother Design protected slow, unclear “wild card” time and removed a traditional KPI from the output – a counterpoint to speed-first branding.

“Transferring something as intangible as psychic power into a brand identity was a chunky challenge that we wanted to get right.”
Jo Tulej, creative director, Mother Design
“By protecting this time, and removing a traditional ‘KPI’ from the output, I believe it gave our client a much richer, robust output.”
Jo Tulej, creative director, Mother Design
